verdict: Affirm's revenue jumped 35% to $1.3B on $14.4B of checkout volume, and net income more than doubled to $164M — its eighth straight profitable quarter — as the Affirm Card more than doubled to 6 million cardholders.

segments.name: Interest income
segments.note: Interest borrowers pay on their loans — the biggest revenue line, up 45% as average loans held for investment grew 38% and average APR rose.

segments.name: Total network revenue
segments.note: Fees merchants and card networks pay Affirm on each purchase — up 23% as GMV grew 34%, with the mix shifting toward direct-to-consumer volume that carries lower network fees.

segments.name: Gain on sales of loans
segments.note: Profit from selling loans to funding partners — up 36% on 27% more loans sold and better sale pricing.

segments.name: Servicing income
segments.note: Fees for servicing loans now owned by others — up 22%, tracking the off-balance-sheet portfolio.

flow.costPlain: Affirm's own 'transaction costs': the $259M provision for credit losses, $134M of funding costs, $169M of processing and servicing, and $83M of losses on loan purchase commitments — what it costs to fund and run each loan.

opex.name: Technology and data analytics
opex.note: Engineers, data scientists and the tech running the platform — up 21% YoY, mostly amortization of software Affirm built and infrastructure for 34% more transactions.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Winning merchants and consumers — includes $51M of enterprise warrant expense tied to big partners.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down 3% YoY as stock-based compensation fell $19M.

follow100Note: The rows before 'Kept as profit' add to $13.00 of profit per $100 of revenue; the $0.01 gap is rounding.

takeaways.title: Checkout volume keeps compounding
takeaways.text: GMV grew 34% to $14.4B — the 12th straight quarter above 30%. Direct-to-consumer volume grew 55% to $5.1B, with Affirm Card GMV up 117% to $3.3B. Active consumers rose 19% to 28.7 million and active merchants 48% to 621,000.

takeaways.title: Profit is scaling faster than revenue
takeaways.text: Revenue less transaction costs rose 36% to $617M, or 4.3% of GMV. Operating income nearly tripled to $187M — a 14.8% margin vs 6.8% a year ago — and adjusted operating income reached $380M, a 30% margin.

takeaways.title: Credit costs are the watch item
takeaways.text: 30+ day delinquencies (ex-Peloton and Pay in 4) ticked up 9 basis points YoY to 2.9%, and the provision for credit losses rose 59% to $259M — faster than revenue — as the loan book grew. Recent loan vintages are tracking toward about 3.5% ultimate net charge-offs, in line with expectations.

oneTimers: Operating income includes $51M of enterprise warrant and share-based expense tied to two big partners, inside sales and marketing — the main reason GAAP operating income ($187M) is about half the adjusted figure ($380M, which also adds back $86M of depreciation and amortization and $56M of stock-based compensation).
footerNote: Affirm reports no gross-profit line; 'transaction costs' — its own non-GAAP measure — is shown as the direct cost, leaving Revenue Less Transaction Costs (RLTC) as the gross-profit bar.
pngFooterNote: Transaction costs are Affirm's own RLTC measure.
